title: Tail Cuff Blood Pressure Determination Protocol
author: Jeff Hodgin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.56eg9be
materials: Setting up Equipment and Software 1.1 Turn on warming platforms. The ideal temperature for blood pressure (BP) monitoring is 30 ~ 35 ̊C. If the mouse tail is too cold, BP will not be read.However, if the warming platform is too hot, mice will be stressed and may lead to severe dehydration or even death. 1.2 Select appropriate mouse holder and warm the holder, too. 1.3 Turn on the CODA Blood Pressure System and then double-click the icon of CODA program on computer.

Blood pressure measurement 3.1 In CODA software, select file and choose new, enter mouse information and the names of experiment and researcher under New select Experiment or Session according to the instructions on the screen. 3.2 Click the “Finish” button will begin blood pressure measurements at once. 3.3 Measure blood pressure for 20 cycles each mouse. 3.4 Release the mouse and put them back to the cage immediately.

steps.title: Prepare the mouse
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in the holder and secure the equipment to the tail.

substeps.instruction: Gently handle the mouse and place it in the holder without forcing.
Carefully attach the end piece of the mouse holder to avoid pinching the tail or other body parts.
Lead the mouse tail through the O-Cuff and then through the VPR-Cuff.
Fasten the cuffs by sliding the hose into the notch on top of the mouse holder.

steps.title: Acclimate the mouse
steps.instruction: Allow the mouse to warm and acclimate in the holder with the tail cuff on for 3-5 minutes, using a blanket to cover the mouse tails.

steps.title: Collect blood pressure data
steps.instruction: Measure blood pressure at the same time each day for a minimum of 3 days and a maximum of 5 consecutive days.

steps.title: Process and export data
steps.instruction: Export the collected data as an excel sheet to the designated folders and calculate the average systolic BP, diastolic BP, and mean arterial pressure (MAP) for each mouse.
